sections.content: Use *más* ... *que* for a greater degree, *menos* ... que for a smaller degree, and *tan* ... *como* for equality. The adjective agrees with the noun it describes.

items.spanish: Este viaje es más barato que el otro.
items.english: This trip is cheaper than the other one.

items.spanish: El hotel es menos cómodo que el alojamiento.
items.english: The hotel is less comfortable than the accommodation.

items.spanish: Ninh Bình es tan bonito como Hanói.
items.english: Ninh Bình is as beautiful as Hanoi.

sections.content: Lock in the pairing: más and menos always close with que, while tan always closes with como — mixing them into tan ... que is one of the most common comparative slips.
